speaker: Doctor
text: That is a concerning combination of symptoms. To understand the neurological progression, have you noticed any changes in your vision or hearing in addition to the forgetfulness and paranoia?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the right leg weakness progressed from one side of the body to the other, or is it strictly unilateral? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain shows disseminated, nonenhancing white matter lesions with no mass effect.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

The MRI findings of nonenhancing white matter lesions in a patient with subacute cognitive decline, behavioral changes, and focal motor deficits are highly suggestive of PML. This is likely due to an immunocompromised state, such as HIV or other causes of cellular immunodeficiency. I will proceed with requesting a CD4 count and HIV test to confirm the underlying cause.

REQUEST TEST: HIV_Status; CD4_Count
